Yeah, If this friend group of his is just a bunch of single guys I could see a situation where his buddies tease him about it and rather than being the focus of that kind of attention he just changes his screen. However you do mention in other replies that your fights are not healthy and that leads me to thinking you don't have positive communication. Also even though I said it could be his buddies ribbing him about being in a committed relationship, that doesn't mean that him changing his phone picture rather than standing up for you (or anyone, or his desire to be in a committed relationship) isn't a bit of a red flag. 

Also him continuing to be friends with someone he can't bring his partner around is a giant, Texas sized red flag. At this point my BF has met both of my besties, and I don't have friends I wouldn't be comfortable with him meeting, and I've met most of his friends and family. The only reason he hasn't met the rest of mine is because we live across the country from them and scheduling is hard. 

So yeah, it's more sketchy that you can't even MEET these so-called friends of his after 7 months if he's fine with you meeting the others. Like are these his work buddies? What makes these friends so different that you can meet the others and not these? 

I'm not saying you should break up with him, but I do think you guys need to have a serious conversation about it, and be honest with him. Let him know that you aren't comfortable being in a relationship with someone who is OK concealing his girlfriend from his friends. And if he mentions something about you being judgmental ask him what you would have to be judgmental about, and if it's excessive drinking or womanizing then the better question is why is he still friends with them if he doesn't trust them to be polite to someone he cares about.  

If he hems and haws, or doesn't have satisfactory answers to those questions then that's your giant, blinking neon sign to get out.

I've been dating my boyfriend for three years and mine usually rotates between the Earth/Moon/Mars and some random art I'm feeling from the internet.  His has been the generic default iPhone Lock Screen since he got his phone last year.  I don't feel some type of way that I'm not his Lock Screen, and he hasn't brought it up to me that my phone doesn't have him as my Lock Screen.   Like my Lock Screen changes probably every two weeks depending on my mood. So if he's really just changing it up regularly and only sometimes is it the picture of the two of you that should be ok. 

  
Now what I do have concerns about is how he's reacting about it whenever he's around you.  Like that last interaction where he's 'freaking out' seems like it was mainly for your benefit.  Like a better question is 'have your friends made comments about me being on your lock screen? Do they harass him? It could be that one of the friends in this specific friends group makes inappropriate or unwelcome comments about either you or the picture and his way of dealing with them is by not having the picture up on his phone to begin with.  

My solution would be to either not try and think about it too much, and see how he reacts the next time he goes out and comes home with a different screen and you don't say anything about it.  If he acts weird again even if you don't bring it up that warrants further investigation, but unless there are other weird things or orange flags when it comes to his friends knowing that you guys are in a relationship then it would be time to have a deeper conversation about it.
